phase1_abstract_interpretation.summary: SECURE: The gossip deduplication logic for data_column_sidecar messages correctly uses the complete composite key (slot, proposer_index, sidecar.index) to prevent equivocation attacks. The implementation properly prevents acceptance of conflicting sidecars with identical keys.

variables.name: slot
variables.usage: First component of composite deduplication key

variables.name: proposerIndex
variables.usage: Second component of composite deduplication key

variables.name: index
variables.usage: Third component of composite deduplication key

variables.name: seenDataColumnCache
variables.usage: Tracks seen data column sidecars to prevent duplicates

data_flow.details: slot = roDataColumn.Slot(), proposerIndex = roDataColumn.ProposerIndex(), index = roDataColumn.DataColumnSidecar.Index
key = computeCacheKey(slot, proposerIndex, index) = Bytes32(slot) || Bytes32(proposerIndex) || Bytes32(index)

data_flow.result: If found: return ValidationIgnore (line 154), else: continue validation

data_flow.details: setSeenDataColumnIndex(slot, proposerIndex, index) called in receiveDataColumnSidecars (subscriber_data_column_sidecar.go:73)
data_flow.timing: Only after full validation passes, before sending to chain

security_properties_verified.evidence: The computeCacheKey function at lines 233-238 correctly concatenates all three components: slot (line 236), proposerIndex (line 237), and index (line 238) using 32-byte encoding for each.

Two sidecars with identical (slot, proposerIndex, index) will produce identical cache keys. The first will pass validation and be marked as seen. The second will be caught by hasSeenDataColumnIndex check at line 153 and return ValidationIgnore.
security_properties_verified.attack_scenario_blocked: If an attacker sends two different sidecars with same (slot, proposerIndex, index) but different content, the second will be ignored, preventing equivocation.

security_properties_verified.evidence: Two sidecars with same (slot, proposerIndex) but different index values will produce different cache keys due to the third component. Both will be accepted as they represent different data columns from the same block.
security_properties_verified.edge_case_handled: Sidecars with indices i1 != i2 for same (slot, proposer) are correctly treated as distinct and both accepted.

security_properties_verified.evidence: The cache is marked AFTER full validation passes (see subscriber_data_column_sidecar.go:73 in receiveDataColumnSidecars), not during validation. This prevents partial state pollution from invalid sidecars.
security_properties_verified.validation_order: Validation check (line 153) -> Full validation -> Cache marking (subscriber:73) -> Chain storage

security_properties_verified.evidence: Line 151-152 comment references the Ethereum consensus spec: '[IGNORE] The sidecar is the first sidecar for the tuple `(block_header.slot, block_header.proposer_index, sidecar.index)`'. The implementation matches this requirement exactly.

initial_state.cache: Empty or contains previously seen (slot, proposerIndex, index) tuples
initial_state.incoming_sidecar: New data column sidecar with components (S, P, I)

state_transitions.condition: Sidecar has (S, P, I) already in cache
state_transitions.next_state: Cache unchanged, sidecar rejected, no equivocation possible

state_transitions.condition: Sidecar has novel (S, P, I) AND passes all validation checks
state_transitions.action: Accept sidecar, mark (S, P, I) as seen, store in chain
state_transitions.next_state: Cache contains (S, P, I), future duplicates will be ignored

state_transitions.condition: Sidecar has novel (S, P, I) BUT fails validation
state_transitions.action: Reject sidecar, do NOT mark as seen
state_transitions.next_state: Cache unchanged, allows valid sidecar with same (S, P, I) to be accepted later

invariants: For any (S, P, I) tuple, at most one data column sidecar will be accepted and stored
Different indices I1 != I2 for same (S, P) are treated as independent entries
Cache key collision only occurs for exact (S, P, I) match due to 96-byte unique encoding

comparison_with_blob_validation.blob_cache_key: Similar pattern using (slot, proposerIndex, blobIndex) composite key
comparison_with_blob_validation.consistency: VERIFIED - Both blob and data column validation use identical three-component deduplication strategy
comparison_with_blob_validation.evidence: Both use hasSeenBlobIndex and hasSeenDataColumnIndex with same parameter structure

formal_verification_notes.key_uniqueness: The 96-byte key (32 bytes × 3 components) ensures no collisions for distinct tuples due to fixed-size encoding via bytesutil.Bytes32
formal_verification_notes.no_integer_overflow: All components (slot, proposerIndex, index) are uint64, bounded by 2^64-1. Bytes32 conversion handles full range without overflow.
formal_verification_notes.no_unbounded_growth: Cache is slotAwareCache which evicts old entries by slot, preventing unbounded memory growth
formal_verification_notes.atomicity: Cache operations (Get/Add) are protected by the underlying cache implementation, no race conditions in deduplication check
